AL5 was reopened after initial ship because the registry/community feature shipped as a typed-but-unwired stub: `loadRegistryIndex` existed, `OFFICIAL_REGISTRY_INDEX` existed, `parseAddSource`/`installSurface` existed — but `surface:add` installed into a repo-root `surfaces/` dir (nothing imported from there), never generated a `register.ts`, never updated the generated index, and never appended to `REGISTERED_SURFACE_MANIFESTS`. Adoption POST 400d; `getSurfaceEntry` returned undefined. All tests were green because tests mocked the registry. Founder caught it: not finished if not wired. Lesson: an install loop that exits without the surface being browsable + adoptable in the actual running app is not done, even if all test assertions pass.

The install->adoptable loop required 3 review rounds, each catching a real defect tests missed: (1) wrong target dir + no registration (surface:add wrote files nowhere the app resolved); (2) runtime TDZ crash (register.ts imported registerSurface from surface-registry.ts creating an ESM cycle — REGISTRY in TDZ on fresh Node process); (3) false-green guard (the lint guard matched the wrong path pattern and passed even when the forbidden import was present). In each case the reviewer ACTUALLY RUNNING the CLI found the defect. Suite-green is not the same as loop-works. For install/CLI flows, the mandatory proof is running the full loop on a real source.

The codegen-mutates-source pattern (surface:add edits a shared .ts array + a generated index) is inherently hard to test honestly: a test can only mock the FS write or assert the string that was written, but not prove the written code compiles + works in the real ESM module graph. Three consecutive false-green guards (different guard shapes, same wrong outcome) confirmed this. The right enforcement for a static import invariant is a static lint rule (no-restricted-imports in eslint.config.ts), not a test asserting file content. Tests prove runtime behavior; lint proves static structure. The static guard can be sanity-broken by writing a fixture violating the rule and confirming lint goes red — which is what AL5-tzdguard-import-chain.test.ts and the __test-fixtures__ do.
